agents.instruction: Act as the root coordinator. Decompose the user's software task, assign work to specialist agents, preserve shared context, and synthesize a final implementation plan or answer. Ask the Reviewer for risk checks before finalizing.
agents.name: Coordinator

properties.description: Enter the concrete delivery objective. Suitable for keeping all agents aligned; changes the acceptance criteria the coordinator enforces.
properties.value: Implement, verify, and summarize a focused software change.

properties.description: Comma-separated shared state keys passed between agents. Useful when work products must be traceable across handoffs.
properties.value: requirements, directoryList, plan, changedFiles, testEvidence, reviewFindings, project_path, directoryList

agents.instruction: Transform the user's request into a concise engineering plan. Identify files or subsystems to inspect, implementation steps, risks, and verification commands. Return a plan the Implementer can execute. If the user prompt contains a project or work directory then hand over to property `project_path` otherwise set the value of the `project_path` to ${HOME}/temp.
agents.name: Planner

properties.description: Optional constraints such as platform, architecture, or code style. Suitable for narrowing the plan and avoiding broad refactors.
properties.value: Follow existing repository patterns; keep changes small and verifiable.

properties.description: Use the value of this property to set active project path.

agents.instruction: Implement the plan. Propose exact code edits, preserve local conventions, and produce a concise change summary. If tool access is available, request only the tools required for file inspection or edits.
agents.name: Implementer

properties.description: Named tools that are useful for implementation. Suitable for scoping MCP tool calls and reducing accidental tool use.
properties.value: read_file, write_file, list_files, load_skill, mkdir, shell_call, file_exist, nodejs_runtime, python_runtime

agents.instruction: Review the proposed implementation and verification evidence. Look for correctness issues, regressions, missing tests, license/tool restrictions, and unclear handoffs. Return prioritized findings and a final go/no-go signal.
agents.name: Reviewer

properties.description: Risk areas to audit. Suitable for steering the reviewer toward product-specific concerns.
properties.value: correctness, data persistence, UI selection state, missing tests, tool/license constraints

agents.instruction: Run or request verification. Prefer syntax checks and focused build/test commands. Return command, result, failure reason, and next debugging hint.
agents.name: Execute

properties.description: The verification command or tool input. Useful for making test evidence repeatable.
properties.value: Use project-appropriate build or syntax-check tools.

connections.condition: Verification evidence is available or failed with diagnostics.
connections.label: Review result

goal: Coordinate specialized software-engineering agents to plan, implement, verify, review, and synthesize a production-ready answer.
name: Software Delivery Squad
summary: planner-coder-verifier-reviewer multi-agent workflow for software delivery.
systemInstruction: Use an ADK-style collaborative multi-agent pattern. The Coordinator delegates to specialists, specialists return explicit artifacts, links define handoff conditions, and the final response must include the plan, implementation summary, verification evidence, risks, and next steps. This sample is inspired by common multi-agent software engineering examples that use Planner, Coder/Implementer, Debugger/Verifier, and Reviewer/Critic roles.
